summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (L8) evaluating whether NAD-precursor (NMN/NR) supplementation after senolytic/SASP clearance yields a smaller tissue ΔNAD than the same precursor without prior clearance — the "subtract-before-add" hypothesis. The claim is pre-registered with a ≥20% shrink margin and is currently classified as NEGATIVE/UNKNOWN because no dedicated ± senolysis residual precursor factorial experiment has been performed. The document synthesizes four published literature anchors and identifies the key untested prediction.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Status
content_blocks.content: Report ID: L8. Status: NEGATIVE. Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Tags: aging, longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Polarity: negative. Vault hold: no. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Related prior: L5/L6/L7 (not proof of precursor residual shrink after senolysis). Kill cost tier: 2. Time to refute: 6 weeks. IP class: subtract-before-add.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim (L8 Hypothesis)
content_blocks.content: After documented senescent-cell / SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, residual tissue ΔNAD from a matched NAD-precursor pulse (NMN/NR class) is smaller than ΔNAD from the same precursor without prior clearance at a matched timepoint. Pre-registered threshold: (ΔNAD_precursor_alone − ΔNAD_precursor_post-senolysis) ≥ 20% of ΔNAD_precursor_alone, or alone wins on a pre-registered superiority test.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Mechanism: 'Subtract-before-add' — clear SASP-driven CD38+ macrophage load first, then pulse the same NAD precursor. CD38 gates age-related NAD decline and NMN fate; SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that drain tissue NAD; senescent/SASP ablation lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD via an NMN-dependent route. Once CD38 load is subtracted, residual precursor salvage headroom shrinks so post-senolysis ΔNAD_precursor < precursor-alone ΔNAD. This is distinct from L7 (CD38i-arm shrink) and L5/L6 (residual arm ranking).

content_blocks.title: Clinical/Scientific Relevance
content_blocks.content: Longevity stacks often add NMN/NR after or with senolytics expecting more NAD. This hypothesis challenges that assumption by predicting that senolytic pre-treatment reduces the incremental NAD benefit of subsequent precursor supplementation. Distinct from L5/L6 (CD38i vs precursor residual ranking) and L7 (same-drug CD38i ± senolysis shrink); no CD38i arm required for L8.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Anchors
content_blocks.content:
Four published literature anchors support the mechanistic basis:
1. PMID 27304511 (Camacho-Pereira 2016, Cell Metab, DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2016.05.006, PMC4911708): Age-related NAD decline requires CD38; CD38 is the major in vivo NMN-degrading activity.
2. PMID 33199924 (Covarrubias 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00305-3, PMC7908681): SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that reduce tissue NAD.
3. PMID 33199925 (Chini 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00298-z, PMC8752031): Senescent/SASP ablation ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD NMN-dependently.
4. PMID 35263032 (Tarragó 2022, Aging Cell, DOI 10.1111/acel.13589, PMC9009115): CD38 inhibitor 78c improves median survival/healthspan in aged mice as monotherapy — not a precursor ± senolysis residual ΔNAD factorial.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed (by opponents): After senolysis, NAD precursor still delivers full monotherapy-class ΔNAD; stacking precursor with/after senolytics always adds NAD; L5–L7 already settled it.
Baseline measured:
- CD38 gates age NAD/NMN fate: LITERATURE (PMID 27304511)
- SASP→CD38+ macrophages→tissue NAD↓: LITERATURE (PMID 33199924)
- Clearance ↓CD38 + partial NAD rebound; ecto-block NMN-dependent: LITERATURE (PMID 33199925)
- 78c aged-mouse benefit: LITERATURE monotherapy (PMID 35263032)
- Same NAD precursor ± senolysis residual ΔNAD factorial: UNKNOWN (soft-complete empty)
- Shrink margin ≥20% of alone-arm Δ: PREDICTION
- L5–L7 do not prove L8: L5/L6 ranked residual arms; L7 tested CD38i residual shrink only.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat L5–L7 as proving L8 — L5/L6 ranked residual CD38i vs precursor; L7 measured CD38i ± senolysis only; precursor residual shrink remains a separate untested claim.
2. Baseline NAD rebound after clearance can shrink absolute ΔNAD even if fractional salvage holds — assay must pre-register residual vs absolute Δ definition.
3. Incomplete clearance: residual CD38+ macrophages can still gate NMN — shrink is not automatic if CD38 load remains; 78c monotherapy ≠ precursor ± senolysis residual panel.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Method and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Method: propose-assay. Refute if: On the pre-registered ± senolysis panel, residual precursor ΔNAD after clearance is not smaller than precursor alone by the ≥20% alone-arm margin (or alone fails superiority) when CD38↓ is verified — especially under incomplete clearance where residual CD38+ load remains high, or when shrink is only an absolute-baseline artifact under the pre-registered residual/fractional definition.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove ± senolysis run-in factorial with matched NAD-precursor pulse: Without the same-drug residual contrast, clearance/ecto-block LITERATURE cannot show precursor ΔNAD shrinks after subtract.
2. Remove documented clearance run-in with CD38↓ / partial NAD rebound verification: Without subtract-first confirmation, the card collapses into generic precursor dosing comparison.
3. Remove L5–L7≠proof + incomplete-clearance + absolute-vs-residual assay discipline: Treating L5–L7 as measured precursor residual, or ignoring residual CD38+ load / baseline rebound artifacts, would invent a factorial result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Human Guidance / Experimental Design Requirements
content_blocks.content: Lock tissue (WAT/liver), clearance verification (CD38 activity + SC/SASP marker), matched NAD-precursor pulse timing, and residual vs absolute ΔNAD definition before claiming shrink; do not treat L5–L7 as proof; no dosing specified.

key_findings: Core hypothesis (L8) is NEGATIVE/UNKNOWN: no dedicated ± senolysis residual NAD-precursor factorial experiment has been performed (soft-complete empty).
Execution status is NOT_RUN — the proposed assay has not been conducted; this is a TRL 1 concept with mechanistic literature support only.

Four published literature anchors establish the mechanistic basis: CD38 gates age NAD/NMN fate (PMID 27304511), SASP induces CD38-high macrophages draining tissue NAD (PMID 33199924), senolytic clearance ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD (PMID 33199925), and 78c CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (PMID 35263032).
Pre-registered threshold: (ΔNAD_precursor_alone − ΔNAD_precursor_post-senolysis) ≥ 20% of ΔNAD_precursor_alone for the hypothesis to be confirmed.
Key gap: the same NAD precursor ± senolysis residual ΔNAD factorial is UNKNOWN — no prior study (including L5/L6/L7) has tested this specific combination.
Critical assay design requirements: pre-register residual vs absolute ΔNAD definition; verify CD38 activity drop post-clearance; lock tissue type (WAT/liver); match NAD-precursor pulse timing.
Kill cost tier 2; estimated time to refute: 6 weeks; IP class: subtract-before-add; vault hold: no.
FTO status is UNKNOWN for the subtract-before-add IP class.
Competing outcome pre-registered: no-shrink / incomplete-clearance / assay-definition failure are valid falsifying outcomes.
